         <dependency>

             <artifactId>spring-aop</artifactId>
         </dependency>
         <dependency>
             <groupId>org.javassist</groupId>
             <artifactId>javassist</artifactId>
         </dependency>

             <groupId>ch.qos.logback</groupId>

         </dependency>

             <scope>test</scope>
         </dependency>
         <dependency>

             <scope>test</scope>
         </dependency>
         <dependency>

             <scope>test</scope>
         </dependency>
         <dependency>

             <scope>test</scope>
         </dependency>
         <dependency>

             <artifactId>javax.servlet-api</artifactId>
             <scope>test</scope>
         </dependency>
     </dependencies>
 
     <build>
         <sourceDirectory>${project.basedir}/src/main/kotlin</sourceDirectory>
         <plugins>
             <plugin>
                 <groupId>org.codehaus.mojo</groupId>
                 <artifactId>build-helper-maven-plugin</artifactId>
                 <version>3.3.0</version>
                 <executions>
                     <execution>
                         <id>add-test-source</id>
                         <phase>generate-test-sources</phase>
                         <goals>
                             <goal>add-test-source</goal>
                         </goals>
                         <configuration>
                             <sources>
                                 <source>src/test/kotlin</source>
                             </sources>
                         </configuration>
                     </execution>
                 </executions>
             </plugin>
 
             <!-- Compile Kotlin -->
             <plugin>
                 <artifactId>kotlin-maven-plugin</artifactId>
                 <groupId>org.jetbrains.kotlin</groupId>
                 <version>${kotlin.version}</version>
                 <executions>
                     <execution>
                         <id>compile</id>
                         <phase>process-sources</phase>
                         <goals>
                             <goal>compile</goal>
                         </goals>
                     </execution>
                     <execution>
                         <id>test-compile</id>
                         <phase>test-compile</phase>
                         <goals>
                             <goal>test-compile</goal>
                         </goals>
                     </execution>
                 </executions>
             </plugin>
 
 
             <plugin>
                 <groupId>org.apache.maven.plugins</groupId>
                 <artifactId>maven-compiler-plugin</artifactId>
                 <version>3.10.1</version>
                 <configuration>
                     <source>1.8</source>
                     <target>1.8</target>
                 </configuration>
             </plugin>
 
             <plugin>
                 <groupId>org.apache.maven.plugins</groupId>
                 <artifactId>maven-surefire-plugin</artifactId>
                 <version>2.22.2</version>
                 <dependencies>
                     <dependency>
                         <groupId>org.apache.maven.surefire</groupId>
                         <artifactId>surefire-junit4</artifactId>
                         <version>2.22.2</version>
                     </dependency>
                 </dependencies>
                 <configuration>
                     <includes>
                         <include>**/*Test.*</include>
                     </includes>
                 </configuration>
             </plugin>
             <plugin>
                 <groupId>org.apache.maven.plugins</groupId>
                 <artifactId>maven-jar-plugin</artifactId>
                 <version>3.2.2</version>
                 <executions>
                     <execution>
                         <id>test-jar</id>
                         <goals>
                             <goal>test-jar</goal>
                         </goals>
                     </execution>
                 </executions>
             </plugin>

             <plugin>
                 <groupId>org.apache.maven.plugins</groupId>
                 <artifactId>maven-enforcer-plugin</artifactId>
                 <version>3.0.0</version>
                 <executions>
                     <execution>
                         <id>enforce</id>
                         <goals>
                             <goal>enforce</goal>
                         </goals>
                         <configuration>
                             <rules>
                                 <dependencyConvergence/>
                             </rules>
                         </configuration>
                     </execution>
                 </executions>
             </plugin>
             <plugin>
                 <groupId>org.sonatype.plugins</groupId>
                 <artifactId>nexus-staging-maven-plugin</artifactId>
                 <version>1.6.13</version>
                 <extensions>true</extensions>
                 <configuration>
                     <serverId>ossrh</serverId>
                     <nexusUrl>https://oss.sonatype.org/</nexusUrl>
                     <autoReleaseAfterClose>true</autoReleaseAfterClose>
                 </configuration>
             </plugin>
         </plugins>
     </build>

{"type":"output_text","text":{"value":"In **graphql-java** versions **17.0+**, specifically starting with version 18.0, the interfaces and APIs around **SchemaDirectiveWiring** and its related wiring environments have changed as part of a wider package and type reorganization and improvement.

Here’s what you need to know:

## `SchemaDirectiveWiringEnvironment` in graphql-java 18.0

In graphql-java 17 and earlier, custom directives could be implemented by providing a `SchemaDirectiveWiring` and operating on the various `*WiringEnvironment` classes such as `SchemaDirectiveWiringEnvironment<T>`.

### Package Change

In graphql-java 18+, the `SchemaDirectiveWiringEnvironment<T>` interface has been **moved to a new package**:
```java
graphql.schema.idl
```
You'd use:
```java
import graphql.schema.idl.SchemaDirectiveWiringEnvironment;
```
### Type Parameter T

The type parameter `<T extends GraphQLSchemaElement>` is still present:
```java
public interface SchemaDirectiveWiringEnvironment<T extends GraphQLSchemaElement>
```
### Usage Example

Here’s how you might use it in **Java** with version 18.0+:

```java
import graphql.schema.idl.SchemaDirectiveWiring;
import graphql.schema.idl.SchemaDirectiveWiringEnvironment;
import graphql.schema.GraphQLFieldDefinition;

public class MyDirectiveWiring implements SchemaDirectiveWiring {
    @Override
    public GraphQLFieldDefinition onField(SchemaDirectiveWiringEnvironment<GraphQLFieldDefinition> env) {
        // You have access to env.getElement(), env.getDirective(), etc.
        return env.getElement(); // Return the field, potentially modified
    }
}
```

Note:
- `env.getElement()`: Gets the element being wired (e.g., a field, object type).
- `env.getDirective()`: Gets the directive definition on that element.
- There are other methods to access context, registry, etc.

### Migration tip

Because of interface and package changes, **if you’re migrating from an earlier version**, update all imports of `SchemaDirectiveWiringEnvironment` and its related classes to `graphql.schema.idl`.

### Reference

See the [graphql-java 18.0 migration guide](https://github.com/graphql-java/graphql-java/releases/tag/v18.0) and [SchemaDirectiveWiringEnvironment JavaDoc](https://www.javadoc.io/doc/com.graphql-java/graphql-java/18.0/graphql/schema/idl/SchemaDirectiveWiringEnvironment.html) for more details.

---

**In summary:**  
In graphql-java 18.0, `SchemaDirectiveWiringEnvironment` is still the type passed to wiring methods, but make sure to import it from `graphql.schema.idl` and update all references if you are upgrading. The way you implement directive wiring remains largely the same.","annotations":null},"bing_searches":null,"annotations":null}

{"type":"output_text","text":{"value":"It looks like you're asking about how to use or find information on the method `getAppliedDirective` in the context of `SchemaDirectiveWiringEnvironment`, possibly related to a version 18.0 of a library (likely graphql-java).

Here's a breakdown of what you might need:

---

## **1. `getAppliedDirective`: Overview**

In **graphql-java**, `getAppliedDirective` is a method associated with objects like `SchemaDirectiveWiringEnvironment`, which enables you to access applied directives on GraphQL schema elements when using schema directive wiring.

---

## **2. `SchemaDirectiveWiringEnvironment`**

- **Type**: An interface in graphql-java.
- **Purpose**: It provides context to the wiring methods, including access to the element (field/object type/etc), the schema, the build environment, and the **applied directive**.

---

## **3. Usage Example** (graphql-java v18.0+)

Supposing you are writing a custom directive:

```java
public class MyDirectiveWiring implements SchemaDirectiveWiring {
    @Override
    public GraphQLFieldDefinition onField(SchemaDirectiveWiringEnvironment<GraphQLFieldDefinition> env) {
        AppliedDirective directive = env.getAppliedDirective();
        // Use directive to change behavior or processing.
        ...
        return env.getElement();
    }
}
```

- `env.getAppliedDirective()` retrieves the **AppliedDirective** from the environment, representing the directive instance with its arguments as attached to the schema element.

---

## **4. Version 18.0**

As of **graphql-java 18.0**, this pattern remains the same and `getAppliedDirective()` is consistently used in custom schema directive wiring implementations .

---

1. package graphql.kickstart.tools
2. 
3. import graphql.Scalars
4. import graphql.introspection.Introspection
5. import graphql.kickstart.tools.directive.SchemaGeneratorDirectiveHelper
6. import graphql.kickstart.tools.util.getDocumentation
7. import graphql.kickstart.tools.util.getExtendedFieldDefinitions
8. import graphql.kickstart.tools.util.unwrap
9. import graphql.language.*
10. import graphql.schema.*
11. import graphql.schema.idl.RuntimeWiring
12. import graphql.schema.idl.ScalarInfo
13. import graphql.schema.visibility.NoIntrospectionGraphqlFieldVisibility
14. import org.slf4j.LoggerFactory
15. import kotlin.reflect.KClass
16. 
17. /**
18.  * Parses a GraphQL Schema and maps object fields to provided class methods.
19.  *
20.  * @author Andrew Potter
21.  */
22. class SchemaParser internal constructor(
23.     scanResult: ScannedSchemaObjects,
24.     private val options: SchemaParserOptions,
25.     private val runtimeWiring: RuntimeWiring
26. ) {
27.     private val log = LoggerFactory.getLogger(javaClass)
28. 
29.     companion object {
30.         @JvmStatic
31.         fun newParser() = SchemaParserBuilder()
32.     }
33. 
34.     private val dictionary = scanResult.dictionary
35.     private val definitions = scanResult.definitions
36.     private val customScalars = scanResult.customScalars
37.     private val rootInfo = scanResult.rootInfo
38.     private val fieldResolversByType = scanResult.fieldResolversByType
39.     private val unusedDefinitions = scanResult.unusedDefinitions
40. 
41.     private val extensionDefinitions = definitions.filterIsInstance<ObjectTypeExtensionDefinition>()
42.     private val inputExtensionDefinitions = definitions.filterIsInstance<InputObjectTypeExtensionDefinition>()
43. 
44.     private val objectDefinitions = (definitions.filterIsInstance<ObjectTypeDefinition>() - extensionDefinitions)
45.     private val inputObjectDefinitions = (definitions.filterIsInstance<InputObjectTypeDefinition>() - inputExtensionDefinitions)
46.     private val enumDefinitions = definitions.filterIsInstance<EnumTypeDefinition>()
47.     private val interfaceDefinitions = definitions.filterIsInstance<InterfaceTypeDefinition>()
48. 
49.     private val unionDefinitions = definitions.filterIsInstance<UnionTypeDefinition>()
50. 
51.     private val permittedTypesForObject: Set<String> = (objectDefinitions.map { it.name } +
52.         enumDefinitions.map { it.name } +
53.         interfaceDefinitions.map { it.name } +
54.         unionDefinitions.map { it.name }).toSet()
55.     private val permittedTypesForInputObject: Set<String> =
56.         (inputObjectDefinitions.map { it.name } + enumDefinitions.map { it.name }).toSet()
57. 
58.     private val codeRegistryBuilder = GraphQLCodeRegistry.newCodeRegistry()
59. 
60.     private val schemaGeneratorDirectiveHelper = SchemaGeneratorDirectiveHelper()
61.     private val schemaDirectiveParameters = SchemaGeneratorDirectiveHelper.Parameters(null, runtimeWiring, null, codeRegistryBuilder)
62. 
63.     /**
64.      * Parses the given schema with respect to the given dictionary and returns GraphQL objects.
65.      */
66.     fun parseSchemaObjects(): SchemaObjects {
67.         if (!options.introspectionEnabled) {
68.             codeRegistryBuilder.fieldVisibility(NoIntrospectionGraphqlFieldVisibility.NO_INTROSPECTION_FIELD_VISIBILITY)
69.         }
70.         // this overrides the above introspection enabled setting obviously... todo: add documentation
71.         options.fieldVisibility?.let { codeRegistryBuilder.fieldVisibility(it) }
72. 
73.         // Create GraphQL objects
74.         val inputObjects: MutableList<GraphQLInputObjectType> = mutableListOf()
75.         inputObjectDefinitions.forEach {
76.             if (inputObjects.none { io -> io.name == it.name }) {
77.                 inputObjects.add(createInputObject(it, inputObjects, mutableSetOf()))
78.             }
79.         }
80.         val interfaces = interfaceDefinitions.map { createInterfaceObject(it, inputObjects) }
81.         val objects = objectDefinitions.map { createObject(it, interfaces, inputObjects) }
82.         val unions = unionDefinitions.map { createUnionObject(it, objects) }
83.         val enums = enumDefinitions.map { createEnumObject(it) }
84. 
85.         // Assign type resolver to interfaces now that we know all of the object types
86.         interfaces.forEach { codeRegistryBuilder.typeResolver(it, InterfaceTypeResolver(dictionary.inverse(), it)) }
87.         unions.forEach { codeRegistryBuilder.typeResolver(it, UnionTypeResolver(dictionary.inverse(), it)) }
88. 
89.         // Find query type and mutation/subscription type (if mutation/subscription type exists)
90.         val queryName = rootInfo.getQueryName()
91.         val mutationName = rootInfo.getMutationName()
92.         val subscriptionName = rootInfo.getSubscriptionName()
93. 
94.         val query = objects.find { it.name == queryName }
95.             ?: throw SchemaError("Expected a Query object with name '$queryName' but found none!")
96.         val mutation = objects.find { it.name == mutationName }
97.             ?: if (rootInfo.isMutationRequired()) throw SchemaError("Expected a Mutation object with name '$mutationName' but found none!") else null
98.         val subscription = objects.find { it.name == subscriptionName }
99.             ?: if (rootInfo.isSubscriptionRequired()) throw SchemaError("Expected a Subscription object with name '$subscriptionName' but found none!") else null
100. 
101.         val additionalObjects = objects.filter { o -> o != query && o != subscription && o != mutation }
102. 
103.         val types = (additionalObjects.toSet() as Set<GraphQLType>) + inputObjects + enums + interfaces + unions
104.         return SchemaObjects(query, mutation, subscription, types, codeRegistryBuilder, rootInfo.getDescription())
105.     }
106. 
107.     /**
108.      * Parses the given schema with respect to the given dictionary and returns a GraphQLSchema
109.      */
110.     fun makeExecutableSchema(): GraphQLSchema = parseSchemaObjects().toSchema()
111. 
112.     /**
113.      * Returns any unused type definitions that were found in the schema
114.      */
115.     @Suppress("unused")
116.     fun getUnusedDefinitions(): Set<TypeDefinition<*>> = unusedDefinitions
117. 
118.     private fun createObject(objectDefinition: ObjectTypeDefinition, interfaces: List<GraphQLInterfaceType>, inputObjects: List<GraphQLInputObjectType>): GraphQLObjectType {
119.         val name = objectDefinition.name
120.         val builder = GraphQLObjectType.newObject()
121.             .name(name)
122.             .definition(objectDefinition)
123.             .description(getDocumentation(objectDefinition, options))
124. 
125.         builder.withDirectives(*buildDirectives(objectDefinition.directives, Introspection.DirectiveLocation.OBJECT))
126. 
127.         objectDefinition.implements.forEach { implementsDefinition ->
128.             val interfaceName = (implementsDefinition as TypeName).name
129.             builder.withInterface(interfaces.find { it.name == interfaceName }
130.                 ?: throw SchemaError("Expected interface type with name '$interfaceName' but found none!"))
131.         }
132. 
133.         objectDefinition.getExtendedFieldDefinitions(extensionDefinitions).forEach { fieldDefinition ->
134.             builder.field { field ->
135.                 createField(field, fieldDefinition, inputObjects)
136.                 codeRegistryBuilder.dataFetcher(
137.                     FieldCoordinates.coordinates(objectDefinition.name, fieldDefinition.name),
138.                     fieldResolversByType[objectDefinition]?.get(fieldDefinition)?.createDataFetcher()
139.                         ?: throw SchemaError("No resolver method found for object type '${objectDefinition.name}' and field '${fieldDefinition.name}', this is most likely a bug with graphql-java-tools")
140.                 )
141. 
142.                 val wiredField = field.build()
143.                 GraphQLFieldDefinition.Builder(wiredField)
144.                     .clearArguments()
145.                     .arguments(wiredField.arguments)
146.             }
147.         }
148. 
149.         val objectType = builder.build()
150.         val directiveHelperParameters = SchemaGeneratorDirectiveHelper.Parameters(null, runtimeWiring, null, codeRegistryBuilder)
151. 
152.         return schemaGeneratorDirectiveHelper.onObject(objectType, directiveHelperParameters)
153.     }
154. 
155.     private fun createInputObject(definition: InputObjectTypeDefinition, inputObjects: List<GraphQLInputObjectType>,
156.                                   referencingInputObjects: MutableSet<String>): GraphQLInputObjectType {
157.         val extensionDefinitions = inputExtensionDefinitions.filter { it.name == definition.name }
158. 
159.         val builder = GraphQLInputObjectType.newInputObject()
160.             .name(definition.name)
161.             .definition(definition)
162.             .extensionDefinitions(extensionDefinitions)
163.             .description(getDocumentation(definition, options))
164. 
165.         builder.withDirectives(*buildDirectives(definition.directives, Introspection.DirectiveLocation.INPUT_OBJECT))
166. 
167.         referencingInputObjects.add(definition.name)
168. 
169.         (extensionDefinitions + definition).forEach {
170.             it.inputValueDefinitions.forEach { inputDefinition ->
171.                 val fieldBuilder = GraphQLInputObjectField.newInputObjectField()
172.                     .name(inputDefinition.name)
173.                     .definition(inputDefinition)
174.                     .description(getDocumentation(inputDefinition, options))
175.                     .apply { inputDefinition.defaultValue?.let { v -> defaultValueLiteral(v) } }
176.                     .type(determineInputType(inputDefinition.type, inputObjects, referencingInputObjects))
177.                     .withDirectives(*buildDirectives(inputDefinition.directives, Introspection.DirectiveLocation.INPUT_FIELD_DEFINITION))
178.                 builder.field(fieldBuilder.build())
179.             }
180.         }
181. 
182.         return schemaGeneratorDirectiveHelper.onInputObjectType(builder.build(), schemaDirectiveParameters)
183.     }
184. 
185.     private fun createEnumObject(definition: EnumTypeDefinition): GraphQLEnumType {
186.         val name = definition.name
187.         val type = dictionary[definition]
188.             ?: throw SchemaError("Expected enum with name '$name' but found none!")
189.         if (!type.unwrap().isEnum) throw SchemaError("Type '$name' is declared as an enum in the GraphQL schema but is not a Java enum!")
190. 
191.         val builder = GraphQLEnumType.newEnum()
192.             .name(name)
193.             .definition(definition)
194.             .description(getDocumentation(definition, options))
195. 
196.         builder.withDirectives(*buildDirectives(definition.directives, Introspection.DirectiveLocation.ENUM))
197. 
198.         definition.enumValueDefinitions.forEach { enumDefinition ->
199.             val enumName = enumDefinition.name
200.             val enumValue = type.unwrap().enumConstants.find { (it as Enum<*>).name == enumName }
201.                 ?: throw SchemaError("Expected value for name '$enumName' in enum '${type.unwrap().simpleName}' but found none!")
202. 
203.             val enumValueDirectives = buildDirectives(enumDefinition.directives, Introspection.DirectiveLocation.ENUM_VALUE)
204.             getDeprecated(enumDefinition.directives).let {
205.                 val enumValueDefinition = GraphQLEnumValueDefinition.newEnumValueDefinition()
206.                     .name(enumName)
207.                     .description(getDocumentation(enumDefinition, options))
208.                     .value(enumValue)
209.                     .deprecationReason(it)
210.                     .withDirectives(*enumValueDirectives)
211.                     .definition(enumDefinition)
212.                     .build()
213. 
214.                 builder.value(enumValueDefinition)
215.             }
216.         }
217. 
218.         return schemaGeneratorDirectiveHelper.onEnum(builder.build(), schemaDirectiveParameters)
219.     }
220. 
221.     private fun createInterfaceObject(interfaceDefinition: InterfaceTypeDefinition, inputObjects: List<GraphQLInputObjectType>): GraphQLInterfaceType {
222.         val name = interfaceDefinition.name
223.         val builder = GraphQLInterfaceType.newInterface()
224.             .name(name)
225.             .definition(interfaceDefinition)
226.             .description(getDocumentation(interfaceDefinition, options))
227. 
228.         builder.withDirectives(*buildDirectives(interfaceDefinition.directives, Introspection.DirectiveLocation.INTERFACE))
229. 
230.         interfaceDefinition.fieldDefinitions.forEach { fieldDefinition ->
231.             builder.field { field -> createField(field, fieldDefinition, inputObjects) }
232.         }
233. 
234.         interfaceDefinition.implements.forEach { implementsDefinition ->
235.             val interfaceName = (implementsDefinition as TypeName).name
236.             builder.withInterface(GraphQLTypeReference(interfaceName))
237.         }
238. 
239.         return schemaGeneratorDirectiveHelper.onInterface(builder.build(), schemaDirectiveParameters)
240.     }
241. 
242.     private fun createUnionObject(definition: UnionTypeDefinition, types: List<GraphQLObjectType>): GraphQLUnionType {
243.         val name = definition.name
244.         val builder = GraphQLUnionType.newUnionType()
245.             .name(name)
246.             .definition(definition)
247.             .description(getDocumentation(definition, options))
248. 
249.         builder.withDirectives(*buildDirectives(definition.directives, Introspection.DirectiveLocation.UNION))
250. 
251.         getLeafUnionObjects(definition, types).forEach { builder.possibleType(it) }
252.         return schemaGeneratorDirectiveHelper.onUnion(builder.build(), schemaDirectiveParameters)
253.     }
254. 
255.     private fun getLeafUnionObjects(definition: UnionTypeDefinition, types: List<GraphQLObjectType>): List<GraphQLObjectType> {
256.         val name = definition.name
257.         val leafObjects = mutableListOf<GraphQLObjectType>()
258. 
259.         definition.memberTypes.forEach {
260.             val typeName = (it as TypeName).name
261. 
262.             // Is this a nested union? If so, expand
263.             val nestedUnion: UnionTypeDefinition? = unionDefinitions.find { otherDefinition -> typeName == otherDefinition.name }
264. 
265.             if (nestedUnion != null) {
266.                 leafObjects.addAll(getLeafUnionObjects(nestedUnion, types))
267.             } else {
268.                 leafObjects.add(types.find { type -> type.name == typeName }
269.                     ?: throw SchemaError("Expected object type '$typeName' for union type '$name', but found none!"))
270.             }
271.         }
272.         return leafObjects
273.     }
274. 
275.     private fun createField(field: GraphQLFieldDefinition.Builder, fieldDefinition: FieldDefinition, inputObjects: List<GraphQLInputObjectType>): GraphQLFieldDefinition.Builder {
276.         field
277.             .name(fieldDefinition.name)
278.             .description(getDocumentation(fieldDefinition, options))
279.             .definition(fieldDefinition)
280.             .apply { getDeprecated(fieldDefinition.directives)?.let { deprecate(it) } }
281.             .type(determineOutputType(fieldDefinition.type, inputObjects))
282. 
283.         fieldDefinition.inputValueDefinitions.forEach { argumentDefinition ->
284.             val argumentBuilder = GraphQLArgument.newArgument()
285.                 .name(argumentDefinition.name)
286.                 .definition(argumentDefinition)
287.                 .description(getDocumentation(argumentDefinition, options))
288.                 .type(determineInputType(argumentDefinition.type, inputObjects, setOf()))
289.                 .apply { argumentDefinition.defaultValue?.let { defaultValueLiteral(it) } }
290.                 .withDirectives(*buildDirectives(argumentDefinition.directives, Introspection.DirectiveLocation.ARGUMENT_DEFINITION))
291. 
292.             field.argument(argumentBuilder.build())
293.         }
294.         field.withDirectives(*buildDirectives(fieldDefinition.directives, Introspection.DirectiveLocation.FIELD_DEFINITION))
295. 
296.         return field
297.     }

299.     private fun buildDirectives(directives: List<Directive>, directiveLocation: Introspection.DirectiveLocation): Array<GraphQLDirective> {
300.         val names = mutableSetOf<String>()
301. 
302.         val output = mutableListOf<GraphQLDirective>()
303.         for (directive in directives) {
304.             if (!names.contains(directive.name)) {
305.                 names.add(directive.name)
306.                 val graphQLDirective = GraphQLDirective.newDirective()
307.                     .name(directive.name)
308.                     .description(getDocumentation(directive, options))
309.                     .comparatorRegistry(runtimeWiring.comparatorRegistry)
310.                     .validLocation(directiveLocation)
311.                     .apply {
312.                         directive.arguments.forEach { arg ->
313.                             argument(GraphQLArgument.newArgument()
314.                                 .name(arg.name)
315.                                 .type(buildDirectiveInputType(arg.value))
316.                                 .valueLiteral(arg.value)
317.                                 .build())
318.                         }
319.                     }
320.                     .build()
321. 
322.                 output.add(graphQLDirective)
323.             }
324.         }
325. 
326.         return output.toTypedArray()
327.     }

329.     private fun buildDirectiveInputType(value: Value<*>): GraphQLInputType? {
330.         when (value) {
331.             is NullValue -> return Scalars.GraphQLString
332.             is FloatValue -> return Scalars.GraphQLFloat
333.             is StringValue -> return Scalars.GraphQLString
334.             is IntValue -> return Scalars.GraphQLInt
335.             is BooleanValue -> return Scalars.GraphQLBoolean
336.             is ArrayValue -> return GraphQLList.list(buildDirectiveInputType(getArrayValueWrappedType(value)))
337.             else -> throw SchemaError("Directive values of type '${value::class.simpleName}' are not supported yet.")
338.         }
339.     }
340. 
341.     private fun getArrayValueWrappedType(value: ArrayValue): Value<*> {
342.         // empty array [] is equivalent to [null]
343.         if (value.values.isEmpty()) {
344.             return NullValue.newNullValue().build()
345.         }
346. 
347.         // get rid of null values
348.         val nonNullValueList = value.values.filter { v -> v !is NullValue }
349. 
350.         // [null, null, ...] unwrapped is null
351.         if (nonNullValueList.isEmpty()) {
352.             return NullValue.newNullValue().build()
353.         }
354. 
355.         // make sure the array isn't polymorphic
356.         val distinctTypes = nonNullValueList
357.             .map { it::class.java }
358.             .distinct()
359. 
360.         if (distinctTypes.size > 1) {
361.             throw SchemaError("Arrays containing multiple types of values are not supported yet.")
362.         }
363. 
364.         // peek at first value, value exists and is assured to be non-null
365.         return nonNullValueList[0]
366.     }

368.     private fun determineOutputType(typeDefinition: Type<*>, inputObjects: List<GraphQLInputObjectType>) =
369.         determineType(GraphQLOutputType::class, typeDefinition, permittedTypesForObject, inputObjects) as GraphQLOutputType

371.     private fun <T : Any> determineType(expectedType: KClass<T>, typeDefinition: Type<*>, allowedTypeReferences: Set<String>, inputObjects: List<GraphQLInputObjectType>): GraphQLType =
372.         when (typeDefinition) {
373.             is ListType -> GraphQLList(determineType(expectedType, typeDefinition.type, allowedTypeReferences, inputObjects))
374.             is NonNullType -> GraphQLNonNull(determineType(expectedType, typeDefinition.type, allowedTypeReferences, inputObjects))
375.             is InputObjectTypeDefinition -> {
376.                 log.info("Create input object")
377.                 createInputObject(typeDefinition, inputObjects, mutableSetOf())
378.             }
379.             is TypeName -> {
380.                 val scalarType = customScalars[typeDefinition.name]
381.                     ?: GRAPHQL_SCALARS[typeDefinition.name]
382.                 if (scalarType != null) {
383.                     scalarType
384.                 } else {
385.                     if (!allowedTypeReferences.contains(typeDefinition.name)) {
386.                         throw SchemaError("Expected type '${typeDefinition.name}' to be a ${expectedType.simpleName}, but it wasn't!  " +

391.             }

393.         }

395.     private fun determineInputType(typeDefinition: Type<*>, inputObjects: List<GraphQLInputObjectType>, referencingInputObjects: Set<String>) =
396.         determineInputType(GraphQLInputType::class, typeDefinition, permittedTypesForInputObject, inputObjects, referencingInputObjects)

398.     private fun <T : Any> determineInputType(expectedType: KClass<T>,
399.                                              typeDefinition: Type<*>, allowedTypeReferences: Set<String>,
400.                                              inputObjects: List<GraphQLInputObjectType>,
401.                                              referencingInputObjects: Set<String>): GraphQLInputType =
402.         when (typeDefinition) {
403.             is ListType -> GraphQLList(determineType(expectedType, typeDefinition.type, allowedTypeReferences, inputObjects))
404.             is NonNullType -> GraphQLNonNull(determineType(expectedType, typeDefinition.type, allowedTypeReferences, inputObjects))
405.             is InputObjectTypeDefinition -> {
406.                 log.info("Create input object")
407.                 createInputObject(typeDefinition, inputObjects, referencingInputObjects as MutableSet<String>)
408.             }
409.             is TypeName -> {
410.                 val scalarType = customScalars[typeDefinition.name]
411.                     ?: GRAPHQL_SCALARS[typeDefinition.name]
412.                 if (scalarType != null) {
413.                     scalarType
414.                 } else {
415.                     if (!allowedTypeReferences.contains(typeDefinition.name)) {
416.                         throw SchemaError("Expected type '${typeDefinition.name}' to be a ${expectedType.simpleName}, but it wasn't!  " +
417.                             "Was a type only permitted for object types incorrectly used as an input type, or vice-versa?")
418.                     }
419.                     val found = inputObjects.filter { it.name == typeDefinition.name }
420.                     if (found.size == 1) {
421.                         found[0]
422.                     } else {
423.                         val filteredDefinitions = inputObjectDefinitions.filter { it.name == typeDefinition.name }
424.                         if (filteredDefinitions.isNotEmpty()) {
425.                             val referencingInputObject = referencingInputObjects.find { it == typeDefinition.name }
426.                             if (referencingInputObject != null) {
427.                                 GraphQLTypeReference(referencingInputObject)
428.                             } else {
429.                                 val inputObject = createInputObject(filteredDefinitions[0], inputObjects, referencingInputObjects as MutableSet<String>)
430.                                 (inputObjects as MutableList).add(inputObject)
431.                                 inputObject
432.                             }
433.                         } else {
434.                             // todo: handle enum type
435.                             GraphQLTypeReference(typeDefinition.name)
436.                         }
437.                     }
438.                 }
439.             }
440.             else -> throw SchemaError("Unknown type: $typeDefinition")
441.         }

443.     /**
444.      * Returns an optional [String] describing a deprecated field/enum.
445.      * If a deprecation directive was defined using the @deprecated directive,
446.      * then a String containing either the contents of the 'reason' argument, if present, or a default
447.      * message defined in [DEFAULT_DEPRECATION_MESSAGE] will be returned. Otherwise, `null` will be returned
448.      * indicating no deprecation directive was found within the directives list.
449.      */
450.     private fun getDeprecated(directives: List<Directive>): String? =
451.         getDirective(directives, "deprecated")?.let { directive ->
452.             (directive.arguments.find { it.name == "reason" }?.value as? StringValue)?.value
453.                 ?: DEFAULT_DEPRECATION_MESSAGE
454.         }
455. 
456.     private fun getDirective(directives: List<Directive>, name: String): Directive? = directives.find {
457.         it.name == name
458.     }
459. }
460. 
461. class SchemaError(message: String, cause: Throwable? = null) : RuntimeException(message, cause)
462. 
463. val GRAPHQL_SCALARS = ScalarInfo.GRAPHQL_SPECIFICATION_SCALARS.associateBy { it.name }
464. 
465. const val DEFAULT_DEPRECATION_MESSAGE = "No longer supported"

1. **Adding Directives in graphql-java-tools:**  
   The typical approach in `graphql-java` is to use `RuntimeWiring` and implement `SchemaDirectiveWiring`, but `graphql-java-tools` builds the schema more abstractly, which makes direct wiring of directives less straightforward.    For directive arguments specifically, the standard SDL lets you define arguments (e.g., `@custom(arg: "value")`), but wiring custom behavior for those arguments requires you to interact with `SchemaDirectiveWiring`. - If you’re hitting limitations and need more advanced directive support (like actually allowing directives on directive arguments in the schema—beyond just mapping annotations), you might need to:
  - Patch the parser and generator code in `graphql-java-tools` yourself.
  - Open an issue or PR in the GitHub repo explaining the use case and proposed changes.
  - Track or contribute to discussions/branches related to directive improvements.

  ```
  interface Character {

  }
  ```

```java
GraphQLInterfaceType characterInterface = GraphQLInterfaceType.newInterface()

    .field(field -> field

    .typeResolver(myTypeResolver)
    .build();
```

1. package graphql.kickstart.tools.util
2. 
3. import graphql.kickstart.tools.GraphQLResolver
4. import graphql.kickstart.tools.SchemaParserOptions
5. import graphql.language.*
6. import graphql.schema.DataFetchingEnvironment
7. import kotlinx.coroutines.CoroutineScope
8. import kotlinx.coroutines.Dispatchers
9. import java.lang.reflect.Method
10. import java.lang.reflect.ParameterizedType
11. import java.lang.reflect.Proxy
12. 
13. /**
14.  * @author Andrew Potter
15.  */
16. 
17. internal typealias GraphQLRootResolver = GraphQLResolver<Void>
18. 
19. internal typealias JavaType = java.lang.reflect.Type
20. internal typealias JavaMethod = Method
21. internal typealias GraphQLLangType = Type<*>
22. 
23. internal fun Type<*>.unwrap(): Type<*> = when (this) {
24.     is NonNullType -> this.type.unwrap()
25.     is ListType -> this.type.unwrap()
26.     else -> this
27. }
28. 
29. internal fun ObjectTypeDefinition.getExtendedFieldDefinitions(extensions: List<ObjectTypeExtensionDefinition>): List<FieldDefinition> {
30.     return this.fieldDefinitions + extensions.filter { it.name == this.name }.flatMap { it.fieldDefinitions }
31. }
32. 
33. internal fun JavaType.unwrap(): Class<out Any> =
34.     if (this is ParameterizedType) {
35.         this.rawType as Class<*>
36.     } else {
37.         this as Class<*>
38.     }
39. 
40. internal fun DataFetchingEnvironment.coroutineScope(): CoroutineScope {
41.     val context: Any? = this.getContext()
42.     return if (context is CoroutineScope) context else CoroutineScope(Dispatchers.Default)
43. }
44. 
45. internal val Class<*>.declaredNonProxyMethods: List<JavaMethod>
46.     get() {
47.         return when {
48.             Proxy.isProxyClass(this) -> emptyList()
49.             else -> this.declaredMethods.toList()
50.         }
51.     }
52. 
53. internal fun getDocumentation(node: AbstractNode<*>, options: SchemaParserOptions): String? =
54.     when {
55.         node is AbstractDescribedNode<*> && node.description != null -> node.description.content
56.         !options.useCommentsForDescriptions -> null
57.         node.comments.isNullOrEmpty() -> null
58.         else -> node.comments.asSequence()
59.             .filter { !it.content.startsWith("#") }
60.             .joinToString("\n") { it.content.trimEnd() }
61.             .trimIndent()
62.     }
63. 
64. /**
65.  * Simple heuristic to check is a method is a trivial data fetcher.
66.  *
67.  * Requirements are:
68.  * prefixed with get
69.  * must have zero parameters
70.  */
71. internal fun isTrivialDataFetcher(method: Method): Boolean {
72.     return (method.parameterCount == 0
73.         && (
74.         method.name.startsWith("get")
75.             || isBooleanGetter(method)))
76. }
77. 
78. private fun isBooleanGetter(method: Method) = (method.name.startsWith("is")
79.     && (method.returnType == java.lang.Boolean::class.java)
80.     || method.returnType == Boolean::class.java)
81. 
82. internal fun String.snakeToCamelCase(): String = split("_").joinToString(separator = "") { it.replaceFirstChar(Char::titlecase) }
83. 
84.

I'm digging into why the `-Xjsr305=ignore` directive isn't resolving the issue. My current hypothesis revolves around the `definition` property within `GraphQLInterfaceType` and `GraphQLFieldDefinition` in graphql-java 18.0. I need to confirm if it's returning `InterfaceTypeDefinition?` directly, which implies explicit nullability in Java.

**Exploring Nullability Source**

My investigation into the `-Xjsr305=ignore` directive continues. I've identified that `GraphQLInterfaceType` itself declares `getDefinition()` with a non-annotated, non-nullable return type in Java. However, I'm now examining its implemented interfaces and superclasses to see if nullability is introduced through inheritance.

**Confirming Nullability Inheritance**

I've pinpointed the source of the nullability issue. It appears a parent interface in `graphql-java 18.0` defines `getDefinition()` as `@Nullable`. This annotation, when inherited, causes Kotlin's compiler to incorrectly infer nullability for the overridden method in `GraphQLInterfaceType`.

**Tracing Nullability Propagation**

I'm still trying to understand how nullability is inferred despite `-Xjsr305=ignore`. It seems the issue isn't directly with JSR-305 annotations in `graphql-java`'s `GraphQLInterfaceType`. I need to investigate alternative nullability annotations like `@Nullable` from JetBrains or Javax, or even internal `graphql` annotations, and see how they might be influencing Kotlin's compiler.

**Shadowing Nullable Definitions**

I'm exploring ways to make tests compile by shadowing the problematic `definition` property. My thought is to create extension properties on `GraphQLFieldDefinition` and `GraphQLInterfaceType` within the `graphql.kickstart.tools` package. The compiler's error message about nullable receivers suggests this approach might resolve the nullability inference issues directly.

**Resolving Null Receiver**

I've discovered the core of the compilation error: the `.definition` property on `GraphQLFieldDefinition` is indeed returning a nullable `FieldDefinition?`. My previous attempts to address this by shadowing might be on the right track, but the direct cause is calling `.sourceLocation` on this nullable `FieldDefinition?` receiver.

**Extending Nullable Types**

I've figured it out! The issue isn't with the nullability of `GraphQLInterfaceType` or `GraphQLFieldDefinition` themselves, but with the return type of their `.definition` property. It's returning `FieldDefinition?` or `InterfaceTypeDefinition?`, which is nullable. Because we can't modify the tests, I'm now investigating writing extension properties directly on these nullable types. This should allow me to safely call `.sourceLocation` or `.implements` without resorting to safe calls or non-null assertions.

**Implementing Nullable Type Extensions**

I've confirmed that the `.definition` property on `GraphQLInterfaceType` and `GraphQLFieldDefinition` returns nullable types. To bypass the need for null checks or assertions, I'm now creating extension properties directly on these nullable types. This should allow safe access to methods like `.sourceLocation` and `.implements`, effectively resolving the compile-time error.

{"type":"output_text","text":{"value":"In **graphql-java**, the `SourceLocation` class represents a location in a source document. It is typically used for error reporting to indicate where in a GraphQL document a problem occurred.

### Constructor

For recent versions of the [`graphql-java`](https://github.com/graphql-java/graphql-java) library (e.g., 17.x and above), the `SourceLocation` constructor looks like:

```java
public SourceLocation(int line, int column)
```

**Parameters:**
- `line`: The line number in the source (1-based).
- `column`: The column number in the source (1-based).

#### There are extended constructors, for example:
```java
public SourceLocation(
    int line, 
    int column, 
    String sourceName
)
```
- `sourceName` is an optional parameter to describe the file or source context.

#### Full list of constructor signatures (as of v21):
```java
public SourceLocation(int line, int column)
public SourceLocation(int line, int column, String sourceName)
public SourceLocation(int line, int column, String sourceName, Map<String, Object> sourcePreview)
```

### Example Usage

```java
SourceLocation loc1 = new SourceLocation(5, 7);
SourceLocation loc2 = new SourceLocation(5, 7, "schema.graphql");
```

#### Reference
- [graphql-java SourceLocation javadoc](https://javadoc.io/doc/com.graphql-java/graphql-java/latest/graphql/language/SourceLocation.html)

If you need the constructor for a specific version or more context (such as deprecations or changes), let me know!","annotations":null},"bing_searches":null,"annotations":null}

{"type":"output_text","text":{"value":"The error message:

```
A definition for directive could not be found
```

in the context of `graphql-java` (version 18 or similar) typically means that you are either using a custom directive (like `@customDirective`) in your GraphQL schema, but you **have not declared it** in your schema definition.

### Explanation

GraphQL directives such as `@deprecated` or `@include` are built-in, but if you introduce your own directive (e.g., `@auth`, `@uppercase`, etc.), you **must declare it** in your schema before using it.

#### Example problem:

```graphql
type Query {
  hello: String @myDirective
}
```

But somewhere in your schema, you **forgot** to add:

```graphql
directive @myDirective on FIELD_DEFINITION
```

So `graphql-java` can't find the definition and throws this error.

---

## How to Fix

1. **Declare the directive in your schema** at the appropriate place:

   ```graphql
   directive @myDirective on FIELD_DEFINITION
   ```

   This line should appear somewhere in your `.graphqls` SDL files _before_ the first use of `@myDirective`.

2. **If you are using a custom directive in your code but not in your schema**, add the directive definition as above.

3. **Check the specific directive** mentioned in the error—make sure it exists in your schema.

---

### Extra: Using Built-in Directives

If you are using only built-in directives (`@include`, `@skip`, etc.), and still get this error, you may have a misconfiguration or a typo in your schema.

---

## Summary

To resolve:

- **Add a directive definition** for every custom directive you use in the schema.
- **Check for typos** if you are using built-in directives.

If you need an example or your directive is more complex (like arguments or multiple locations), let me know!","annotations":null},"bing_searches":null,"annotations":null}

A directive provides a way to annotate fields or types in a GraphQL schema with additional metadata or behavior. You can define a directive in SDL like this:

```graphql
directive @auth(role: String!) on FIELD_DEFINITION
```

And use it, for example:

```graphql
type Employee {
  salary: Float @auth(role: "manager")
}
```

To create a directive programmatically in graphql-java, you would typically use the `GraphQLDirective` class:

```java
GraphQLDirective upperCaseDirective = GraphQLDirective.newDirective()
    .name("uppercase")
    .description("Directs the executor to uppercase this field")
    .validLocations(FIELD)
    .build();
```

You then "wire" the behavior to your directive using `SchemaDirectiveWiring` to make it functional. The core concept is that a directive definition tells the schema where the directive can be used and what arguments it takes, but the logic or enforcement of what a directive *does* must be implemented in Java code through wiring.

- **Original Design**: The `GraphQLDirective` and `GraphQLArgument` classes were used both for directive definitions (as declared in schema) and for instances when directives were actually applied to schema or query elements. This was later identified as a modeling mistake, as these concepts are distinct in the GraphQL specification【3:0†source】【3:9†source】.

    - `GraphQLAppliedDirective`

  These are now used to represent directives as they are actually applied to specific schema elements. The legacy usage of `GraphQLDirective` for both definitions and applications is deprecated, and the library is moving toward cleaner separation:
  - `GraphQLDirective`: Represents the directive definition only.
  - `GraphQLAppliedDirective`: Represents an instance of a directive applied to a schema element.

- **Migration Guidance**: 
  - Use the new `getAppliedXXX` methods instead of the older `getDirectiveXXX` methods when accessing applied directives.
  - The older classes/methods remain for backward compatibility but will be removed in a future version.
  - Be aware that schema and query visitors may be called twice (once for each style), so code that traverses the schema should switch to the new API.

1. package graphql.kickstart.tools
2. 
3. import graphql.Scalars
4. import graphql.introspection.Introspection
5. import graphql.kickstart.tools.directive.SchemaGeneratorDirectiveHelper
6. import graphql.kickstart.tools.util.getDocumentation
7. import graphql.kickstart.tools.util.getExtendedFieldDefinitions
8. import graphql.kickstart.tools.util.unwrap
9. import graphql.language.*
10. import graphql.schema.*
11. import graphql.schema.idl.RuntimeWiring
12. import graphql.schema.idl.ScalarInfo
13. import graphql.schema.visibility.NoIntrospectionGraphqlFieldVisibility
14. import org.slf4j.LoggerFactory
15. import kotlin.reflect.KClass
16. 
17. /**
18.  * Parses a GraphQL Schema and maps object fields to provided class methods.
19.  *
20.  * @author Andrew Potter
21.  */
22. class SchemaParser internal constructor(
23.     scanResult: ScannedSchemaObjects,
24.     private val options: SchemaParserOptions,
25.     private val runtimeWiring: RuntimeWiring
26. ) {
27.     private val log = LoggerFactory.getLogger(javaClass)
28. 
29.     companion object {
30.         @JvmStatic
31.         fun newParser() = SchemaParserBuilder()
32.     }
33. 
34.     private val dictionary = scanResult.dictionary
35.     private val definitions = scanResult.definitions
36.     private val customScalars = scanResult.customScalars
37.     private val rootInfo = scanResult.rootInfo
38.     private val fieldResolversByType = scanResult.fieldResolversByType
39.     private val unusedDefinitions = scanResult.unusedDefinitions
40. 
41.     private val extensionDefinitions = definitions.filterIsInstance<ObjectTypeExtensionDefinition>()
42.     private val inputExtensionDefinitions = definitions.filterIsInstance<InputObjectTypeExtensionDefinition>()
43. 
44.     private val objectDefinitions = (definitions.filterIsInstance<ObjectTypeDefinition>() - extensionDefinitions)
45.     private val inputObjectDefinitions = (definitions.filterIsInstance<InputObjectTypeDefinition>() - inputExtensionDefinitions)
46.     private val enumDefinitions = definitions.filterIsInstance<EnumTypeDefinition>()
47.     private val interfaceDefinitions = definitions.filterIsInstance<InterfaceTypeDefinition>()
48. 
49.     private val unionDefinitions = definitions.filterIsInstance<UnionTypeDefinition>()
50. 
51.     private val permittedTypesForObject: Set<String> = (objectDefinitions.map { it.name } +
52.         enumDefinitions.map { it.name } +
53.         interfaceDefinitions.map { it.name } +
54.         unionDefinitions.map { it.name }).toSet()
55.     private val permittedTypesForInputObject: Set<String> =
56.         (inputObjectDefinitions.map { it.name } + enumDefinitions.map { it.name }).toSet()
57. 
58.     private val codeRegistryBuilder = GraphQLCodeRegistry.newCodeRegistry()
59. 
60.     private val schemaGeneratorDirectiveHelper = SchemaGeneratorDirectiveHelper()
61.     private val schemaDirectiveParameters = SchemaGeneratorDirectiveHelper.Parameters(null, runtimeWiring, null, codeRegistryBuilder)
62. 
63.     /**
64.      * Parses the given schema with respect to the given dictionary and returns GraphQL objects.
65.      */
66.     fun parseSchemaObjects(): SchemaObjects {
67.         if (!options.introspectionEnabled) {
68.             codeRegistryBuilder.fieldVisibility(NoIntrospectionGraphqlFieldVisibility.NO_INTROSPECTION_FIELD_VISIBILITY)
69.         }
70.         // this overrides the above introspection enabled setting obviously... todo: add documentation
71.         options.fieldVisibility?.let { codeRegistryBuilder.fieldVisibility(it) }
72. 
73.         // Create GraphQL objects
74.         val inputObjects: MutableList<GraphQLInputObjectType> = mutableListOf()
75.         inputObjectDefinitions.forEach {
76.             if (inputObjects.none { io -> io.name == it.name }) {
77.                 inputObjects.add(createInputObject(it, inputObjects, mutableSetOf()))
78.             }
79.         }
80.         val interfaces = interfaceDefinitions.map { createInterfaceObject(it, inputObjects) }
81.         val objects = objectDefinitions.map { createObject(it, interfaces, inputObjects) }
82.         val unions = unionDefinitions.map { createUnionObject(it, objects) }
83.         val enums = enumDefinitions.map { createEnumObject(it) }
84. 
85.         // Assign type resolver to interfaces now that we know all of the object types
86.         interfaces.forEach { codeRegistryBuilder.typeResolver(it, InterfaceTypeResolver(dictionary.inverse(), it)) }
87.         unions.forEach { codeRegistryBuilder.typeResolver(it, UnionTypeResolver(dictionary.inverse(), it)) }
88. 
89.         // Find query type and mutation/subscription type (if mutation/subscription type exists)
90.         val queryName = rootInfo.getQueryName()
91.         val mutationName = rootInfo.getMutationName()
92.         val subscriptionName = rootInfo.getSubscriptionName()
93. 
94.         val query = objects.find { it.name == queryName }
95.             ?: throw SchemaError("Expected a Query object with name '$queryName' but found none!")
96.         val mutation = objects.find { it.name == mutationName }
97.             ?: if (rootInfo.isMutationRequired()) throw SchemaError("Expected a Mutation object with name '$mutationName' but found none!") else null
98.         val subscription = objects.find { it.name == subscriptionName }
99.             ?: if (rootInfo.isSubscriptionRequired()) throw SchemaError("Expected a Subscription object with name '$subscriptionName' but found none!") else null
100. 
101.         val additionalObjects = objects.filter { o -> o != query && o != subscription && o != mutation }
102. 
103.         val types = (additionalObjects.toSet() as Set<GraphQLType>) + inputObjects + enums + interfaces + unions
104.         return SchemaObjects(query, mutation, subscription, types, codeRegistryBuilder, rootInfo.getDescription())
105.     }
106. 
107.     /**
108.      * Parses the given schema with respect to the given dictionary and returns a GraphQLSchema
109.      */
110.     fun makeExecutableSchema(): GraphQLSchema = parseSchemaObjects().toSchema()
111. 
112.     /**
113.      * Returns any unused type definitions that were found in the schema
114.      */
115.     @Suppress("unused")
116.     fun getUnusedDefinitions(): Set<TypeDefinition<*>> = unusedDefinitions
117. 
118.     private fun createObject(objectDefinition: ObjectTypeDefinition, interfaces: List<GraphQLInterfaceType>, inputObjects: List<GraphQLInputObjectType>): GraphQLObjectType {
119.         val name = objectDefinition.name
120.         val builder = GraphQLObjectType.newObject()
121.             .name(name)
122.             .definition(objectDefinition)
123.             .description(getDocumentation(objectDefinition, options))
124. 
125.         builder.withDirectives(*buildDirectives(objectDefinition.directives, Introspection.DirectiveLocation.OBJECT))
126. 
127.         objectDefinition.implements.forEach { implementsDefinition ->
128.             val interfaceName = (implementsDefinition as TypeName).name
129.             builder.withInterface(interfaces.find { it.name == interfaceName }
130.                 ?: throw SchemaError("Expected interface type with name '$interfaceName' but found none!"))
131.         }
132. 
133.         objectDefinition.getExtendedFieldDefinitions(extensionDefinitions).forEach { fieldDefinition ->
134.             builder.field { field ->
135.                 createField(field, fieldDefinition, inputObjects)
136.                 codeRegistryBuilder.dataFetcher(
137.                     FieldCoordinates.coordinates(objectDefinition.name, fieldDefinition.name),
138.                     fieldResolversByType[objectDefinition]?.get(fieldDefinition)?.createDataFetcher()
139.                         ?: throw SchemaError("No resolver method found for object type '${objectDefinition.name}' and field '${fieldDefinition.name}', this is most likely a bug with graphql-java-tools")
140.                 )
141. 
142.                 val wiredField = field.build()
143.                 GraphQLFieldDefinition.Builder(wiredField)
144.                     .clearArguments()
145.                     .arguments(wiredField.arguments)
146.             }
147.         }
148. 
149.         val objectType = builder.build()
150.         val directiveHelperParameters = SchemaGeneratorDirectiveHelper.Parameters(null, runtimeWiring, null, codeRegistryBuilder)
151. 
152.         return schemaGeneratorDirectiveHelper.onObject(objectType, directiveHelperParameters)
153.     }
154. 
155.     private fun createInputObject(definition: InputObjectTypeDefinition, inputObjects: List<GraphQLInputObjectType>,
156.                                   referencingInputObjects: MutableSet<String>): GraphQLInputObjectType {
157.         val extensionDefinitions = inputExtensionDefinitions.filter { it.name == definition.name }
158. 
159.         val builder = GraphQLInputObjectType.newInputObject()
160.             .name(definition.name)
161.             .definition(definition)
162.             .extensionDefinitions(extensionDefinitions)
163.             .description(getDocumentation(definition, options))
164. 
165.         builder.withDirectives(*buildDirectives(definition.directives, Introspection.DirectiveLocation.INPUT_OBJECT))
166. 
167.         referencingInputObjects.add(definition.name)
168. 
169.         (extensionDefinitions + definition).forEach {
170.             it.inputValueDefinitions.forEach { inputDefinition ->
171.                 val fieldBuilder = GraphQLInputObjectField.newInputObjectField()
172.                     .name(inputDefinition.name)
173.                     .definition(inputDefinition)
174.                     .description(getDocumentation(inputDefinition, options))
175.                     .apply { inputDefinition.defaultValue?.let { v -> defaultValueLiteral(v) } }
176.                     .type(determineInputType(inputDefinition.type, inputObjects, referencingInputObjects))
177.                     .withDirectives(*buildDirectives(inputDefinition.directives, Introspection.DirectiveLocation.INPUT_FIELD_DEFINITION))
178.                 builder.field(fieldBuilder.build())
179.             }
180.         }
181. 
182.         return schemaGeneratorDirectiveHelper.onInputObjectType(builder.build(), schemaDirectiveParameters)
183.     }
184. 
185.     private fun createEnumObject(definition: EnumTypeDefinition): GraphQLEnumType {
186.         val name = definition.name
187.         val type = dictionary[definition]
188.             ?: throw SchemaError("Expected enum with name '$name' but found none!")
189.         if (!type.unwrap().isEnum) throw SchemaError("Type '$name' is declared as an enum in the GraphQL schema but is not a Java enum!")
190. 
191.         val builder = GraphQLEnumType.newEnum()
192.             .name(name)
193.             .definition(definition)
194.             .description(getDocumentation(definition, options))
195. 
196.         builder.withDirectives(*buildDirectives(definition.directives, Introspection.DirectiveLocation.ENUM))
197. 
198.         definition.enumValueDefinitions.forEach { enumDefinition ->
199.             val enumName = enumDefinition.name
200.             val enumValue = type.unwrap().enumConstants.find { (it as Enum<*>).name == enumName }
201.                 ?: throw SchemaError("Expected value for name '$enumName' in enum '${type.unwrap().simpleName}' but found none!")
202. 
203.             val enumValueDirectives = buildDirectives(enumDefinition.directives, Introspection.DirectiveLocation.ENUM_VALUE)
204.             getDeprecated(enumDefinition.directives).let {
205.                 val enumValueDefinition = GraphQLEnumValueDefinition.newEnumValueDefinition()
206.                     .name(enumName)
207.                     .description(getDocumentation(enumDefinition, options))
208.                     .value(enumValue)
209.                     .deprecationReason(it)
210.                     .withDirectives(*enumValueDirectives)
211.                     .definition(enumDefinition)
212.                     .build()
213. 
214.                 builder.value(enumValueDefinition)
215.             }
216.         }
217. 
218.         return schemaGeneratorDirectiveHelper.onEnum(builder.build(), schemaDirectiveParameters)
219.     }

221.     private fun createInterfaceObject(interfaceDefinition: InterfaceTypeDefinition, inputObjects: List<GraphQLInputObjectType>): GraphQLInterfaceType {
222.         val name = interfaceDefinition.name
223.         val builder = GraphQLInterfaceType.newInterface()
224.             .name(name)
225.             .definition(interfaceDefinition)
226.             .description(getDocumentation(interfaceDefinition, options))
227. 
228.         builder.withDirectives(*buildDirectives(interfaceDefinition.directives, Introspection.DirectiveLocation.INTERFACE))
229. 
230.         interfaceDefinition.fieldDefinitions.forEach { fieldDefinition ->
231.             builder.field { field -> createField(field, fieldDefinition, inputObjects) }
232.         }
233. 
234.         interfaceDefinition.implements.forEach { implementsDefinition ->
235.             val interfaceName = (implementsDefinition as TypeName).name
236.             builder.withInterface(GraphQLTypeReference(interfaceName))
237.         }
238. 
239.         return schemaGeneratorDirectiveHelper.onInterface(builder.build(), schemaDirectiveParameters)
240.     }

242.     private fun createUnionObject(definition: UnionTypeDefinition, types: List<GraphQLObjectType>): GraphQLUnionType {
243.         val name = definition.name
244.         val builder = GraphQLUnionType.newUnionType()
245.             .name(name)
246.             .definition(definition)
247.             .description(getDocumentation(definition, options))
248. 
249.         builder.withDirectives(*buildDirectives(definition.directives, Introspection.DirectiveLocation.UNION))
250.

252.         return schemaGeneratorDirectiveHelper.onUnion(builder.build(), schemaDirectiveParameters)

255.     private fun getLeafUnionObjects(definition: UnionTypeDefinition, types: List<GraphQLObjectType>): List<GraphQLObjectType> {
256.         val name = definition.name
257.         val leafObjects = mutableListOf<GraphQLObjectType>()
258. 
259.         definition.memberTypes.forEach {
260.             val typeName = (it as TypeName).name
261. 
262.             // Is this a nested union? If so, expand
263.             val nestedUnion: UnionTypeDefinition? = unionDefinitions.find { otherDefinition -> typeName == otherDefinition.name }
264. 
265.             if (nestedUnion != null) {
266.                 leafObjects.addAll(getLeafUnionObjects(nestedUnion, types))
267.             } else {
268.                 leafObjects.add(types.find { type -> type.name == typeName }
269.                     ?: throw SchemaError("Expected object type '$typeName' for union type '$name', but found none!"))
270.             }
271.         }
272.         return leafObjects
273.     }

275.     private fun createField(field: GraphQLFieldDefinition.Builder, fieldDefinition: FieldDefinition, inputObjects: List<GraphQLInputObjectType>): GraphQLFieldDefinition.Builder {
276.         field
277.             .name(fieldDefinition.name)
278.             .description(getDocumentation(fieldDefinition, options))
279.             .definition(fieldDefinition)
280.             .apply { getDeprecated(fieldDefinition.directives)?.let { deprecate(it) } }
281.             .type(determineOutputType(fieldDefinition.type, inputObjects))
282. 
283.         fieldDefinition.inputValueDefinitions.forEach { argumentDefinition ->
284.             val argumentBuilder = GraphQLArgument.newArgument()
285.                 .name(argumentDefinition.name)
286.                 .definition(argumentDefinition)
287.                 .description(getDocumentation(argumentDefinition, options))
288.                 .type(determineInputType(argumentDefinition.type, inputObjects, setOf()))
289.                 .apply { argumentDefinition.defaultValue?.let { defaultValueLiteral(it) } }
290.                 .withDirectives(*buildDirectives(argumentDefinition.directives, Introspection.DirectiveLocation.ARGUMENT_DEFINITION))
291. 
292.             field.argument(argumentBuilder.build())
293.         }
294.         field.withDirectives(*buildDirectives(fieldDefinition.directives, Introspection.DirectiveLocation.FIELD_DEFINITION))
295. 
296.         return field
297.     }

299.     private fun buildDirectives(directives: List<Directive>, directiveLocation: Introspection.DirectiveLocation): Array<GraphQLDirective> {
300.         val names = mutableSetOf<String>()
301. 
302.         val output = mutableListOf<GraphQLDirective>()
303.         for (directive in directives) {
304.             if (!names.contains(directive.name)) {
305.                 names.add(directive.name)
306.                 val graphQLDirective = GraphQLDirective.newDirective()
307.                     .name(directive.name)
308.                     .description(getDocumentation(directive, options))
309.                     .comparatorRegistry(runtimeWiring.comparatorRegistry)
310.                     .validLocation(directiveLocation)
311.                     .apply {
312.                         directive.arguments.forEach { arg ->
313.                             argument(GraphQLArgument.newArgument()
314.                                 .name(arg.name)
315.                                 .type(buildDirectiveInputType(arg.value))
316.                                 .valueLiteral(arg.value)
317.                                 .build())
318.                         }
319.                     }
320.                     .build()
321. 
322.                 output.add(graphQLDirective)
323.             }
324.         }
325. 
326.         return output.toTypedArray()
327.     }

329.     private fun buildDirectiveInputType(value: Value<*>): GraphQLInputType? {
330.         when (value) {
331.             is NullValue -> return Scalars.GraphQLString
332.             is FloatValue -> return Scalars.GraphQLFloat
333.             is StringValue -> return Scalars.GraphQLString
334.             is IntValue -> return Scalars.GraphQLInt
335.             is BooleanValue -> return Scalars.GraphQLBoolean
336.             is ArrayValue -> return GraphQLList.list(buildDirectiveInputType(getArrayValueWrappedType(value)))
337.             else -> throw SchemaError("Directive values of type '${value::class.simpleName}' are not supported yet.")
338.         }
339.     }
340. 
341.     private fun getArrayValueWrappedType(value: ArrayValue): Value<*> {
342.         // empty array [] is equivalent to [null]
343.         if (value.values.isEmpty()) {
344.             return NullValue.newNullValue().build()
345.         }
346. 
347.         // get rid of null values
348.         val nonNullValueList = value.values.filter { v -> v !is NullValue }
349. 
350.         // [null, null, ...] unwrapped is null
351.         if (nonNullValueList.isEmpty()) {
352.             return NullValue.newNullValue().build()
353.         }
354. 
355.         // make sure the array isn't polymorphic
356.         val distinctTypes = nonNullValueList
357.             .map { it::class.java }
358.             .distinct()
359. 
360.         if (distinctTypes.size > 1) {
361.             throw SchemaError("Arrays containing multiple types of values are not supported yet.")
362.         }
363. 
364.         // peek at first value, value exists and is assured to be non-null
365.         return nonNullValueList[0]
366.     }

368.     private fun determineOutputType(typeDefinition: Type<*>, inputObjects: List<GraphQLInputObjectType>) =
369.         determineType(GraphQLOutputType::class, typeDefinition, permittedTypesForObject, inputObjects) as GraphQLOutputType

371.     private fun <T : Any> determineType(expectedType: KClass<T>, typeDefinition: Type<*>, allowedTypeReferences: Set<String>, inputObjects: List<GraphQLInputObjectType>): GraphQLType =
372.         when (typeDefinition) {
373.             is ListType -> GraphQLList(determineType(expectedType, typeDefinition.type, allowedTypeReferences, inputObjects))
374.             is NonNullType -> GraphQLNonNull(determineType(expectedType, typeDefinition.type, allowedTypeReferences, inputObjects))
375.             is InputObjectTypeDefinition -> {
376.                 log.info("Create input object")
377.                 createInputObject(typeDefinition, inputObjects, mutableSetOf())
378.             }
379.             is TypeName -> {
380.                 val scalarType = customScalars[typeDefinition.name]
381.                     ?: GRAPHQL_SCALARS[typeDefinition.name]
382.                 if (scalarType != null) {
383.                     scalarType
384.                 } else {
385.                     if (!allowedTypeReferences.contains(typeDefinition.name)) {
386.                         throw SchemaError("Expected type '${typeDefinition.name}' to be a ${expectedType.simpleName}, but it wasn't!  " +
387.                             "Was a type only permitted for object types incorrectly used as an input type, or vice-versa?")
388.                     }
389.                     inputObjects.find { it.name == typeDefinition.name } ?: GraphQLTypeReference(typeDefinition.name)
390.                 }
391.             }
392.             else -> throw SchemaError("Unknown type: $typeDefinition")
393.         }

395.     private fun determineInputType(typeDefinition: Type<*>, inputObjects: List<GraphQLInputObjectType>, referencingInputObjects: Set<String>) =
396.         determineInputType(GraphQLInputType::class, typeDefinition, permittedTypesForInputObject, inputObjects, referencingInputObjects)
397. 
398.     private fun <T : Any> determineInputType(expectedType: KClass<T>,
399.                                              typeDefinition: Type<*>, allowedTypeReferences: Set<String>,
400.                                              inputObjects: List<GraphQLInputObjectType>,
401.                                              referencingInputObjects: Set<String>): GraphQLInputType =
402.         when (typeDefinition) {
403.             is ListType -> GraphQLList(determineType(expectedType, typeDefinition.type, allowedTypeReferences, inputObjects))
404.             is NonNullType -> GraphQLNonNull(determineType(expectedType, typeDefinition.type, allowedTypeReferences, inputObjects))
405.             is InputObjectTypeDefinition -> {
406.                 log.info("Create input object")
407.                 createInputObject(typeDefinition, inputObjects, referencingInputObjects as MutableSet<String>)
408.             }
409.             is TypeName -> {
410.                 val scalarType = customScalars[typeDefinition.name]
411.                     ?: GRAPHQL_SCALARS[typeDefinition.name]
412.                 if (scalarType != null) {
413.                     scalarType
414.                 } else {
415.                     if (!allowedTypeReferences.contains(typeDefinition.name)) {
416.                         throw SchemaError("Expected type '${typeDefinition.name}' to be a ${expectedType.simpleName}, but it wasn't!  " +
417.                             "Was a type only permitted for object types incorrectly used as an input type, or vice-versa?")
418.                     }
419.                     val found = inputObjects.filter { it.name == typeDefinition.name }
420.                     if (found.size == 1) {
421.                         found[0]
422.                     } else {
423.                         val filteredDefinitions = inputObjectDefinitions.filter { it.name == typeDefinition.name }
424.                         if (filteredDefinitions.isNotEmpty()) {
425.                             val referencingInputObject = referencingInputObjects.find { it == typeDefinition.name }
426.                             if (referencingInputObject != null) {
427.                                 GraphQLTypeReference(referencingInputObject)
428.                             } else {
429.                                 val inputObject = createInputObject(filteredDefinitions[0], inputObjects, referencingInputObjects as MutableSet<String>)
430.                                 (inputObjects as MutableList).add(inputObject)
431.                                 inputObject
432.                             }
433.                         } else {
434.                             // todo: handle enum type
435.                             GraphQLTypeReference(typeDefinition.name)
436.                         }
437.                     }
438.                 }
439.             }
440.             else -> throw SchemaError("Unknown type: $typeDefinition")
441.         }

443.     /**
444.      * Returns an optional [String] describing a deprecated field/enum.
445.      * If a deprecation directive was defined using the @deprecated directive,
446.      * then a String containing either the contents of the 'reason' argument, if present, or a default
447.      * message defined in [DEFAULT_DEPRECATION_MESSAGE] will be returned. Otherwise, `null` will be returned
448.      * indicating no deprecation directive was found within the directives list.
449.      */
450.     private fun getDeprecated(directives: List<Directive>): String? =
451.         getDirective(directives, "deprecated")?.let { directive ->
452.             (directive.arguments.find { it.name == "reason" }?.value as? StringValue)?.value
453.                 ?: DEFAULT_DEPRECATION_MESSAGE
454.         }
455. 
456.     private fun getDirective(directives: List<Directive>, name: String): Directive? = directives.find {
457.         it.name == name
458.     }
459. }
460. 
461. class SchemaError(message: String, cause: Throwable? = null) : RuntimeException(message, cause)
462. 
463. val GRAPHQL_SCALARS = ScalarInfo.GRAPHQL_SPECIFICATION_SCALARS.associateBy { it.name }
464. 
465. const val DEFAULT_DEPRECATION_MESSAGE = "No longer supported"
